source_text: Quid postremo de ipso serpente dicetur? Diabolum maledictione illa punitum, an hoc commune reptile animal opinaris? Id est, illam sententiam quae ait ad serpentem: Maledictus tu ab omnibus pecoribus, et ab omnibus bestiis quae sunt super terram; super pectus et ventrem tuum ambulabis, et terram manducabis omnibus diebus vitae tuae [n178] , in diaboli supplicio, an bestiae huius quae vernis caloribus educitur de cavernis, arbitraris impletam? Si in huius serpentis, cuius species in corpus enode porrigitur atque ob illius culpae meritum dicas eam factam esse terrifagam; ergo et omnibus bestiis tradux iniquitatis incumbit, quam putas nisi per libidinem coeuntium non posse deduci; fitque ut etiam serpentum libidinem, iamque inde irrationabilium animantium, asseras a diabolo fuisse plantatam, retectaque sententia Manichaei nobis carmen inclangas. Sin autem quidquid ad serpentem dicitur, intellegibiliter in diabolo profitearis impletum; annues sine dubio, nec hoc quod ibi pro ultione profertur, indicium nunc reorum esse serpentum, nec diabolum terram edere corporaliter; sed etsi tunc ministerium draconis arripuit, atque hoc quasi telum, quo ad vulnerandum hominem usus fuerat, severitas postea paterna confregit; tamen peccatum in solius agentis voluntate resedisse. Cibos autem et spinas et sudores primo fuisse naturaliter instituta, post in aliquibus aucta iudicialiter, ad nostram vero aetatem sine peccati illius admiratione venisse; res tam apertae sunt, ut longiore penitus assertione non egeant.
pass_a_gloss: Finally what will be said about the serpent himself? Do you opine the devil punished by that curse, or this common creeping animal? That is, that sentence which says to the serpent: Cursed are you from all cattle, and from all beasts which are upon the earth; upon your breast and belly you will walk, and you will eat earth all the days of your life, do you judge it fulfilled in the devil's punishment, or of this beast which in spring heats is led out from caverns? If in this serpent, whose appearance is stretched into a knotless body, and you say it was made earth-fleeing on account of the desert of that fault; therefore a tradux of iniquity hangs upon all beasts also, which you think cannot be led down except through the lust of those coupling; and it is done that you assert even the lust of serpents, and from there of irrational living beings, was planted by the devil, and the sentence of Manichaeus having been uncovered you would chant a song to us. But if you profess whatever is said to the serpent was intelligibly fulfilled in the devil; you will grant without doubt, neither that what is brought forth there for vengeance is now an indication of guilty serpents, nor that the devil eats earth corporally; but even if then he snatched the ministry of a dragon, and this as a weapon, which he had used for wounding the human, a paternal severity afterward broke; nevertheless sin resided in the will of the agent alone. But that foods and thorns and sweats were first instituted naturally, afterward in some increased judicially, but came to our age without an admiration of that sin; the things are so open that they thoroughly do not need a longer assertion.

lemmas.lexica: Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil
LS naturalis; Blaise malum naturale=evil as a nature
LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS libido; Blaise pudenda libido vs nuptiae

pass_b_english: What, finally, will be said about the serpent itself? Do you think that curse punished the devil or this ordinary crawling animal? The pronouncement says to the serpent: ‘You are cursed beyond all cattle and all beasts upon the earth. You shall go upon your breast and belly and eat earth all the days of your life’ (Genesis 3:14). Do you think it was fulfilled in the devil’s punishment, or in the beast that spring warmth draws out of its holes?

If in this serpent, whose form stretches into a body without joints, and if you say that fault’s desert made it an earth-eater, then inherited iniquity burdens all beasts too. You think such transmission can occur only through the desire of those coupling. It follows that you must assert the devil planted the desire of serpents and hence of irrational animals. With your position exposed, you will blare Mani’s tune at us.

But if you acknowledge that everything said to the serpent was fulfilled spiritually in the devil, you will undoubtedly agree that the punishment spoken there neither proves present-day serpents guilty nor means the devil bodily eats earth. Even if he then enlisted the serpent’s service, and fatherly severity afterward broke it like the weapon he had used to wound humanity, sin still remained solely in the agent’s will.

Foods, thorns, and sweat were first established naturally, afterward increased judicially in certain cases, and have reached our own age [without that sin itself being passed on]. These matters are so plain that they require no lengthy defense.

choices.why: Julian's pudenda libido is the appetite accompanying union, not a created substance of sin.
Julian's definition of sin is an act of will. Keep 'will' rather than later 'free will' system language unless liberum arbitrium is present.
Julian's Manichaean charge: an evil that is a nature, not a will's act.
